titulo: The complete genitive: Dialogue and reading

aula.objetivo: Form the genitive singular and plural and use it for absence, possession, quantity, origin and the most frequent prepositions.

blocos.titulo: The second use: POSSESSION ("the book of...")
blocos.explicacao: The second use of the genitive is possession. It is the English "of" or 's. Compare. Notice: in Russian the first noun (the thing owned) stays in the nominative. The second noun (the owner) goes into the genitive. The "of" is not a separate word; it is the ending of the second noun. Structure: [thing owned, nominative] + [owner, genitive]. Examples in full sentences. Notice: the first noun (кни́га, дом, и́мя, центр, цвет, му́зыка, кры́ша, дверь) stays in the nominative. The second noun (Ива́на, ма́мы, ма́льчика, го́рода, мо́ря, компози́тора, до́ма, ко́мнаты) goes into the genitive. It is the owner. The magic question is "whose is it?" and the answer goes into the genitive. "Whose book? Ivan's." → Ива́на. Careful with the order: English can say "Ivan's book" (owner first), but Russian always puts the thing first and the owner after it, like English "the book of Ivan".

blocos.titulo: The genitive with "нет" in sentences without у меня
blocos.explicacao: The word нет can also be used without у меня. It then means "there is not", "there is no". Notice: the object still goes into the genitive. Нет always takes the genitive, whether or not there is a «у меня». In context:

tabelas.titulo: The genitive with "нет" in sentences without у меня
The genitive with "нет" in sentences without у меня

blocos.explicacao: The mistakes English speakers WILL make with the genitive. Mistake 1: using the nominative instead of the genitive after «нет». Wrong: У меня́ нет кни́га. Right: У меня́ нет кни́ги. Нет always takes the genitive, without exception. Mistake 2: forgetting that feminine -а becomes -ы (or -и after г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ). Wrong: У меня́ нет кни́гы. Right: У меня́ нет кни́ги. (кни́га has a г before the -а, so it is -и.) Mistake 3: forgetting that feminine -я becomes -и. Wrong: У меня́ нет семья́. Right: У меня́ нет семьи́. Mistake 4: forgetting that feminine -ь becomes -и. Wrong: У меня́ нет дверь. Right: У меня́ нет две́ри. Mistake 5: forgetting that -ия becomes -ии. Wrong: Э́то центр Росси́е. Right: Э́то центр Росси́и (-ия always becomes -ии). Mistake 6: forgetting that -мя becomes -мени. Wrong: У меня́ нет вре́мя. Right: У меня́ нет вре́мени. Mistake 7: confusing the genitive with the animate accusative. For masculine animate nouns the genitive and the accusative have the same form (-а/-я), so it is easy to mix them up. But the function differs. Accusative: the object of the action. Я ви́жу дру́га. (I see my friend.) Genitive: possession or negation. У меня́ нет дру́га. (I have no friend.) The form is the same but the context is different. Don't worry about telling them apart for now; just know that after нет it is always genitive. Mistake 8: putting the thing owned in the genitive instead of the owner. Wrong: Ива́н кни́га (meaning "Ivan's book"). Right: Кни́га Ива́на. The thing owned (кни́га) stays in the nominative. The owner (Ива́н) goes into the genitive (Ива́на). Mistake 9: thinking every English "of" becomes a genitive. English "of" has many senses: possession ("the book of Ivan"), origin ("I am from Chicago"), material ("a table of wood"), subject ("we speak of music"). In Russian each sense has its own structure. The genitive covers possession and some origins. But "a wooden table" is an adjective (деревя́нный стол), not a genitive. For now, focus on the genitive of possession. Mistake 10: getting the stress wrong. Some words move their stress in the genitive: окно́ → окна́ (the stress moves), вода́ → воды́ (the stress moves), рука́ → руки́ (the stress moves). There is no fixed rule. You have to listen and memorise.

blocos.titulo: Sentences and summary table of the genitive singular
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Full sentences with the genitive. Here are real sentences, so you can see the genitive at work. STEP 2: A word of reassurance: you are finishing the hard part. Before closing this lesson, a pause. Listen to what I am about to say. You are finishing the tedious part of Russian. The essential grammar ends here. You have already learned: the alphabet. The gender of nouns. The gender of adjectives. Verbs in the present, past and future. The nominative, accusative, prepositional, dative and instrumental cases. And now the first half of the genitive. Only one thing is missing: the second half of the genitive (plural, numbers, prepositions). We do that in lesson 28. After that you will have all 6 cases of Russian. What comes next is not harder, it is richer: vocabulary, expressions, culture, immersion. You will be able to read, write, listen and speak Russian at A1/A2 level. The learner's mistake is to think the advanced stage is the hard one. In Russian the hard part is the basic structure, because it is abstract, full of rules and full of exceptions. Once you master the structure, everything else flows. You already have the structure. One lesson left, in two parts. And after that, Russian will be yours. STEP 3: Summary table: the genitive singular.

linhas.ru: — Здравствуйте! Мне нужен килограмм сыра и бутылка воды.
linhas.pt: — Hello! I need a kilo of cheese and a bottle of water.
linhas.audio: Здравствуйте! Мне нужен килограмм сыра и бутылка воды.

linhas.pt: — All right. Do you need bread?

linhas.ru: — А яблоки? У нас много яблок.
linhas.audio: А яблоки? У нас много яблок.

linhas.ru: — Да, пожалуйста, килограмм яблок. Сколько стоит?
linhas.pt: — Yes, please, a kilo of apples. How much is it?
linhas.audio: Да, пожалуйста, килограмм яблок. Сколько стоит?

linhas.ru: — Сыр — сто рублей, вода — тридцать, яблоки — пятьдесят.
linhas.pt: — The cheese costs a hundred rubles, the water thirty and the apples fifty.
linhas.audio: Сыр — сто рублей, вода — тридцать, яблоки — пятьдесят.

linhas.pt: — All right, here is the money. Thank you!

blocos.ru: В холодильнике много еды. Там есть килограмм сыра, бутылка молока и много яблок. Хлеба нет, поэтому мне нужно идти в магазин. Я иду из дома в магазин, а потом из магазина домой.
blocos.pt: There is a lot of food in the fridge. There is a kilo of cheese, a bottle of milk and many apples. There is no bread, so I need to go to the store. I go from home to the store and then from the store back home.

blocos.enunciado: Make a shopping list out loud: «Мне нужен килограмм … бутылка … Сколько стоит?»
